citation: Liard E, et al. Impact of reconstruction kernel variability on segmentation consistency in low-dose thoracic CT. Medical Imaging 2026: Image Processing 2026:29. doi:10.1117/12.3085743
modality_and_design: Low-dose non-gated chest CT; paired soft/hard kernel reconstructions of the SAME session (NLST, 9,529 pairs, 9,519 subjects); TotalSegmentator, 84 thoracic regions
structure_measured: 84 thoracic regions incl. heart; thyroid gland
reported_repeatability: Qualitative/graphical: Bland-Altman and Dice; heart reported as more robust to kernel variation than thyroid gland; Siemens lowest kernel-related segmentation variability. No per-structure percentage volume difference is given in the text (results presented as figures).
relevance_to_10pct_threshold: CLOSEST EXTERNAL ANALOGUE to the present design: same-session paired kernels, same segmentation tool family, same organ class. Supports the direction of our heart result but provides no numeric margin.
crossref_title: Impact of reconstruction kernel variability on segmentation consistency in low-dose thoracic CT

citation: Hamelink I, et al. Repeatability of AI-based, automatic measurement of vertebral and cardiovascular imaging biomarkers in low-dose chest CT: the ImaLife cohort. European Radiology 2025;35:3833-3841. doi:10.1007/s00330-024-11328-9
modality_and_design: Low-dose non-gated chest CT, short-interval repeat scan (mean 3.9 months), 632 participants, AI-Rad Companion
structure_measured: Heart volume (chambers + pericardial fat); aortic diameters; vertebral; CAC volume
reported_repeatability: Relative difference baseline vs repeat: <4% for vertebral and aortic measurements; 7.5% for heart volume; 28.5% for coronary artery calcium volume. ICC>0.9 for all biomarkers in adequately segmented cases. Heart segmentation adequate in only 53.5%.
relevance_to_10pct_threshold: PRIMARY ANCHOR for the 10% threshold. Non-gated chest CT, automated heart volume, true test-retest: 7.5% relative difference is the best available estimate of the irreducible interscan floor for the same measurement class, and sits just below 10%.
crossref_title: Repeatability of AI-based, automatic measurement of vertebral and cardiovascular imaging biomarkers in low-dose chest CT: the ImaLife cohort

citation: Bartlett EC, et al. Defining growth in small pulmonary nodules using volumetry: results from a “coffee-break” CT study and implications for current nodule management guidelines. European Radiology 2021;32:1912-1920. doi:10.1007/s00330-021-08302-0
modality_and_design: Same-day repeat ('coffee-break') chest CT, 45 adults, 100 solid nodules 28-170 mm3, commercial volumetry
reported_repeatability: Limits of agreement for relative volume difference -16.4% to +14.6%; mean difference 0.90%; authors propose a 15% volume increase as the threshold for true growth.
relevance_to_10pct_threshold: Establishes the ~15% same-day test-retest limit-of-agreement convention for automated CT volumetry of small structures; 10% is inside (i.e. stricter than) this interval.
crossref_title: Defining growth in small pulmonary nodules using volumetry: results from a “coffee-break” CT study and implications for current nodule management guidelines

citation: Athelogou M, et al. Algorithm Variability in the Estimation of Lung Nodule Volume From Phantom CT Scans: Results of the QIBA 3A Public Challenge. Academic Radiology 2016;23:940-952. doi:10.1016/j.acra.2016.02.018
modality_and_design: Anthropomorphic phantom CT, multiple semi-automated algorithms, QIBA challenge
reported_repeatability: Repeatability coefficient 9.0% over nodules meeting the QIBA Profile; 18.4% overall. 84% of volume measurements of QIBA-compliant tumours within 15% of true volume.
relevance_to_10pct_threshold: Provides the formal QIBA repeatability-coefficient framing. The 9.0% QIBA-compliant repeatability coefficient is the closest published number to our 10% threshold and is the standards-body reference point.
crossref_title: Algorithm Variability in the Estimation of Lung Nodule Volume From Phantom CT Scans: Results of the QIBA 3A Public Challenge

citation: Buckler AJ, et al. Inter-Method Performance Study of Tumor Volumetry Assessment on Computed Tomography Test-Retest Data. Academic Radiology 2015;22:1393-1408. doi:10.1016/j.acra.2015.08.007
modality_and_design: Clinical thoracic CT test-retest, multi-algorithm challenge
reported_repeatability: Intra-algorithm repeatability ranged 13% (best) to 100% (worst); inter-algorithm reproducibility 58% for the four best-performing groups. One-fifth to one-half of total variability was independent of the algorithm.
relevance_to_10pct_threshold: Shows that for automated CT volumetry the algorithm is often NOT the dominant variance source, which is the premise of treating 10% as a practical ceiling rather than an equivalence margin.
crossref_title: Inter-Method Performance Study of Tumor Volumetry Assessment on Computed Tomography Test-Retest Data

citation: Skoog S, et al. Effect of Reconstruction Kernel and Virtual Monoenergetic Imaging on Segmentation-Based Measurement of Coronary Plaque Volume With Photon-Counting CT. Investigative Radiology 2025;60:602-608. doi:10.1097/rli.0000000000001167
modality_and_design: Photon-counting coronary CTA, 50 participants + phantom; kernels Bv48 vs Bv64, 0.2 vs 0.4 mm
reported_repeatability: Sharper kernel (Bv64 vs Bv48) significantly INCREASED non-calcified plaque volume (P<0.005); 0.2 mm slice thickness reduced calcified plaque volume vs 0.4 mm (P<0.005). Virtual monoenergetic level had no effect.
relevance_to_10pct_threshold: Direct evidence that kernel choice shifts segmentation-based cardiovascular volume measurements, and that kernel and slice thickness act on different structures - exactly the separation our kernel-only / thickness strata enforce.
crossref_title: Effect of Reconstruction Kernel and Virtual Monoenergetic Imaging on Segmentation-Based Measurement of Coronary Plaque Volume With Photon-Counting CT

citation: Erdal BS, et al. Are quantitative features of lung nodules reproducible at different CT acquisition and reconstruction parameters?. PLOS ONE 2020;15:e0240184. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0240184
modality_and_design: Raw-data re-reconstruction of 23 nodules under 320 acquisition/reconstruction conditions (4 doses x 10 kernels x 8 thicknesses, 0.6-5.0 mm)
reported_repeatability: Volumetric reproducibility DECREASES as slice thickness increases, while histogram/texture reproducibility improves; balanced standardisation of acquisition parameters is required for concomitant volumetric and radiomic reproducibility.
relevance_to_10pct_threshold: Supports the pre-specified separation of kernel and thickness arms and the expectation that thickness effects on volume exceed kernel effects.
crossref_title: Are quantitative features of lung nodules reproducible at different CT acquisition and reconstruction parameters?

citation: Jordan DW, et al. Quantitative CT reconstruction kernel harmonization for multi‐site lung cancer screening. Journal of Applied Clinical Medical Physics 2025;26. doi:10.1002/acm2.70325
modality_and_design: ACR CT accreditation phantom; MTF/NPS matching across 6 scanner models, 3 manufacturers; QIBA Small Lung Nodule profile conformance
reported_repeatability: Medium-sharp kernels with matched MTF/NPS conformed to the QIBA Small Lung Nodule profile; one medium-smooth iterative kernel and one lung kernel did NOT conform.
relevance_to_10pct_threshold: Shows kernel non-equivalence is a recognised, profile-level quantitative CT problem - i.e. our research question has a standards precedent, and kernel identity alone does not guarantee quantitative interchangeability.
crossref_title: Quantitative CT reconstruction kernel harmonization for multi‐site lung cancer screening
crossref_journal: Journal of Applied Clinical Medical Physics

citation: Ghadri JR, et al. Inter-scan variability of coronary artery calcium scoring assessed on 64-multidetector computed tomography vs. dual-source computed tomography: a head-to-head comparison. European Heart Journal 2011;32:1865-1874. doi:10.1093/eurheartj/ehr157
modality_and_design: ECG-gated cardiac CT, 30 patients scanned on two scanners within <100 days
structure_measured: Coronary calcium Agatston, mass and volume scores
reported_repeatability: Intra-scan (inter-observer) coefficient of variation 2.0-4.7%; inter-scanner coefficient of variation 15.1% (Agatston), 21.6% (mass), 44.9% (volume); volume COV improved to 11.5% after cross-vendor re-analysis in one software.
relevance_to_10pct_threshold: Brackets the threshold from the other side: a purely analytic (same-image) step costs 2-5%, while changing the acquisition/analysis platform costs 15-45%. 10% lies between the two, which is the intended interpretive position.
crossref_title: Inter-scan variability of coronary artery calcium scoring assessed on 64-multidetector computed tomography vs. dual-source computed tomography: a head-to-head comparison

citation: Horiguchi J, et al. Effect of Heart Rate and Body Mass Index on the Interscan and Interobserver Variability of Coronary Artery Calcium Scoring at Prospective ECG-Triggered 64-Slice CT. Korean Journal of Radiology 2009;10:340. doi:10.3348/kjr.2009.10.4.340
modality_and_design: Prospective ECG-triggered 64-slice CT, 110 patients scanned twice
structure_measured: Coronary calcium volume and mass scores
reported_repeatability: Mean/median interscan variability 11%/6% by volume and 11%/6% by mass; Agatston 16%/9%. Mean/median interobserver variability 10%/4%.
relevance_to_10pct_threshold: Independent interscan estimate for a cardiac CT volumetric measure: mean ~11%, median ~6%. Again places 10% at the boundary between measurement noise and a real shift.
crossref_title: Effect of Heart Rate and Body Mass Index on the Interscan and Interobserver Variability of Coronary Artery Calcium Scoring at Prospective ECG-Triggered 64-Slice CT

citation: Paixao ARM, et al. Defining coronary artery calcium concordance and repeatability - Implications for development and change: The Dallas Heart Study. Journal of Cardiovascular Computed Tomography 2017;11:347-353. doi:10.1016/j.jcct.2017.06.004
modality_and_design: Duplicate CAC scans obtained minutes apart, 2,888 participants
reported_repeatability: Binary (0 vs >0) concordance 91%; 95% repeatability bounds given as explicit score-dependent formulas (for CAC<=100 AU: 5.6*sqrt(CAC)+0.3*CAC-3.1).
relevance_to_10pct_threshold: Methodological precedent for deriving a change threshold empirically from same-session repeat scans rather than asserting one - the approach our Reviewer-2 response commits to for any future equivalence claim.
crossref_title: Defining coronary artery calcium concordance and repeatability - Implications for development and change: The Dallas Heart Study

citation: Wang M, et al. Quantifying the impact of slice thickness on cardiovascular risk stratification in lung cancer screening: a multi-center “RESCUE” study. Quantitative Imaging in Medicine and Surgery 2026;16:568-568. doi:10.21037/qims-2026-1-0318
modality_and_design: Paired thin (1.0-2.0 mm) vs standard (5.0 mm) reconstructions of the same acquisition; 2,914 patients across four datasets including NLST and TotalSegmentator cohort
reported_repeatability: 19.0% of an internal cohort reclassified from CAC=0 on 5.0 mm to CAC>0 on 1.0 mm; 10.2% of NLST participants reclassified using 2.0 mm. Weighted kappa for risk category 0.705-0.816.
relevance_to_10pct_threshold: Same-acquisition paired-reconstruction design applied to a cardiac measure, with a clinically meaningful reclassification rate - the strongest external support for the claim that reconstruction parameters alone change cardiovascular readouts.
crossref_title: Quantifying the impact of slice thickness on cardiovascular risk stratification in lung cancer screening: a multi-center “RESCUE” study
crossref_journal: Quantitative Imaging in Medicine and Surgery

citation: El Rahal D, et al. TotalSegmentator-AI for aortic segmentation in CT: Reliable performance in normal anatomy but limited utility in pathological aortic disease. European Journal of Radiology Open 2026;16:100772. doi:10.1016/j.ejro.2026.100772
modality_and_design: 60 CTA scans, 6 categories (young, elderly, aneurysm, dissection, venous phase, non-contrast); TotalSegmentator without manual correction
reported_repeatability: Median qualitative segmentation quality 4 [IQR 4-5]; 77% rated good or excellent; poorest in dissection (3 [IQR 3-4]) and aneurysm (4 [IQR 3-4]); inter-reader kappa 0.72.
relevance_to_10pct_threshold: Tool-specific validity context: TotalSegmentator aortic output is adequate in normal anatomy, which is the regime of most of our pairs, but degrades with pathology - a limit on generalising our aorta result.
crossref_title: TotalSegmentator-AI for aortic segmentation in CT: Reliable performance in normal anatomy but limited utility in pathological aortic disease

citation: Iraqi N, et al. Interscan reproducibility of computed tomography derived coronary plaque volume measurements. Journal of Cardiovascular Computed Tomography 2024;18:583-592. doi:10.1016/j.jcct.2024.09.009
modality_and_design: Coronary CTA performed twice at 1-h interval with identical protocols, 101 patients, semi-automated software
structure_measured: Coronary plaque volume (total, non-calcified, calcified, low-density non-calcified)
reported_repeatability: Interscan Pearson correlation 0.93-0.99 for total/non-calcified/calcified plaque, 0.74-0.77 for low-density non-calcified plaque; agreement better per-patient than per-vessel or per-lesion; authors describe overall reproducibility as modest.
relevance_to_10pct_threshold: Demonstrates that for cardiovascular CT volumetry, correlation can be excellent while agreement is only modest - the reason our paper leads with percentage difference and CI rather than ICC/correlation.
crossref_title: Interscan reproducibility of computed tomography derived coronary plaque volume measurements
